- Model tends to overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.7), often overshooting by 2–5% in the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimates prices when sentiment is low (<0.3) or shows strong downward momentum, especially if recent price drops are steep.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — model reacts 2–3 days too late to sentiment turning points.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to historical mean too quickly, ignoring volatility clustering; true outcomes often show extended drifts after sharp moves.
- Overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment >0.85) — model forecasts peak too early and then drops sharply, missing the “rebound” phase.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the horizon (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is volatile, then underestimate later (last 10–15 days) when sentiment stabilizes or turns negative.
- Sentiment >0.85 correlates with higher forecast error — model fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility, especially in the 10–20 day window.
